questions.solution:
(a) - This sentence is in active voice. The subject (attentive waiter) will perform the action (will serve).

(b) - This sentence is in active voice as well. The subject (attentive waiter) spoke and will be performing the action (will be serving).

(c) - This sentence is in active voice. The subject (attentive waiter) performed the action (served).

(d) - This sentence is in passive voice. The focus is on the meal (the receiver of the action), and the doer of the action (attentive waiter) is mentioned with the preposition "by."

In passive voice constructions, the typical pattern is: Object + a form of "to be" + past participle ('served' in this case) + by + the doer of the action (optional). Option (d) fits this pattern, making it the correct answer.

questions.solution:
•The above sentence is an interrogative sentence starting with a question word (why, when, how, where, etc.).

The subject and object of the passive sentence should become the object and subject of the active sentence respectively.

While making the sentence active, we need to put the suitable helping verb after the question word according to the new subject.

Use the correct form of the main verb according to the tense instead of the past participle.

Remove preposition ‘by’.

•Use the following syntax for the above sentence-

Passive voice- Question word + was/were + subject + not + V3 + by + object + other + ?

Active voice - Question word + did not + new subject + V3 + new object + other + ?

Hence, the correct active voice form is 'Why didn't any of the team members take Shekhar seriously?'

Hence, option b) is correct.
